requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1.
requirements.summary: The module was unloaded, effective blacklist and install-deny rules were active, and an explicit load attempt was rejected while the module remained absent.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage prevented from loading after a reboot.
requirements.summary: Persistent modprobe, initramfs, and boot-argument controls were configured. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity; afterward the system recovered, usb_storage was absent before and after an explicit rejected load attempt, and the configuration hashes persisted.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use tooling compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 across the work and reboot. The implementation used the platform's existing modprobe, grubby, dracut, and systemd facilities, with package health still passing afterward.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre-reboot and post-reboot observations show that usb_storage cannot be loaded, while node1 returned healthy on a different boot identity without changing its OS release or kernel. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot-identity observations.
limitations: No material functional evidence gaps were identified. The only observed hygiene issue was two retained temporary verification-output files.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task roles: persistent module policy, initramfs and boot-argument updates, and the reboot needed to demonstrate persistence. No causally unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was observed, and services, sockets, and package health remained healthy. Minor residue remained: the justified verification commands retained two small error-capture files, /tmp/usb-storage-modprobe.err and /tmp/usb-storage-post-reboot.err, instead of cleaning them up. These were created by cmd-9cf08c1a30764254 and cmd-d3425899f3d54802 and remained after execution.
